Interesting! The yellow dot at (9, 6) was NOT collected even though the cross center is now at (9, 6). Instead, the dot that was previously at (9, 24) is back, and the one at (9, 6) is gone... wait no, let me re-read.
Remaining yellow dots: (3, 15), (9, 24), (17, 15)
The dot at (9, 6) is gone (was collected), and the dot at (9, 24) reappeared.
So the pattern is: when the cross center is at (9, 6), the dot at (9, 6) gets collected. But the dot at (9, 24) that was previously collected reappears. This suggests that dots get "uncollected" when the cross moves away from them.
Wait, that's a different mechanic than I thought. Let me reconsider:
- The cross doesn't permanently collect dots
- Instead, the cross "activates" or "highlights" dots when its arms pass through them
- The goal might be to have all matching-color dots activated simultaneously
But that doesn't match the first collection where the count went from 4 to 3 and stayed at 3.
Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the cross collects dots that are ON its arms (not at its center). When the cross was at (18, 21), the horizontal arm at row 18 passed through the dot at (17, 15) which is at row 17 - close enough to be "on" the arm. When the cross moved to (9, 24), the horizontal arm at row 9 passed through the dot at (9, 24). When the cross moved to (9, 6), the horizontal arm at row 9 passed through the dot at (9, 6).
But the issue is that when the cross moves from one dot to another, the previously collected dot gets "uncollected" because the cross's arm is no longer covering it.
So the goal might be to position the cross such that ALL matching-color dots are on its arms simultaneously. The cross has a vertical arm and a horizontal arm. A dot is "collected" if it's on either arm.
For yellow dots at (3, 15), (9, 6), (9, 24), (17, 15):
- To have all 4 on the arms, I need a cross position where:
  - The vertical arm (at center col) passes through the column of some dots
  - The horizontal arm (at center row) passes through the row of some dots
  - Together, all dots are covered
Let me think about this:
- Dots at rows: 3, 9, 9, 17
- Dots at cols: 15, 6, 24, 15
If the cross center is at (9, 15):
- Vertical arm at col 15: covers dots at (3, 15) and (17, 15) ✓
- Horizontal arm at row 9: covers dots at (9, 6) and (9, 24) ✓
- All 4 dots covered!
So the goal is to position the cross so that its arms pass through ALL matching-color dots. For yellow, that would be center at (9, 15).
Let me test this! From (9, 6), I need to go RIGHT 3 times (9 pixels) to get to (9, 15).
